title: Bible Story: Abraham Welcomes Visitors

answerNotes.TENT: Fabric shelter supported by poles. This scene follows Genesis 18:1–15; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.TREE: Trees have woody trunks and branches. Familiar garden trees may provide fruit, flowers, or shade, sometimes all three.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.FOOT: A foot is a body part and also a unit of length. A shoe clue points to the body meaning rather than twelve inches.
answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.FLOUR: Flour is ground grain used in baking. The fine powder is different from whole kernels even when both come from the same crop.
answerNotes.SON: Son names a male child in a family. The same word applies to the relationship when the child has grown into an adult.
answerNotes.ABRAHAM: Sarah's husband in Genesis. This scene follows Genesis 18:1–15; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.ANGEL: Angel means a heavenly messenger in the Bible stories. Decorative angel figures are representations rather than the story characters themselves.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.OIL: Oil has different uses in different scenes. It can be a cooking ingredient, lamp fuel, or part of a story about caring for a traveler.
answerNotes.JACOB: Joseph's father in Genesis. This scene follows Genesis 28:10–22; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.LADDER: Climbing frame with rungs. This scene follows Genesis 28:10–22; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.COAT: Cold-weather outer garment. This scene follows Genesis 37:1–11; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.GRAIN: Grain can mean an edible seed or the pattern of wood fibers. The food and woodworking scenes use different senses of the same word.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.STAR: A star can mean a distant sun or a pointed decorative shape. Christmas ornaments represent the shape rather than an actual celestial object.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.SHEEP: Sheep are farm animals valued for wool and other products. A lamb is a young sheep, and an ewe is an adult female.
answerNotes.SON: Son names a male child in a family. The same word applies to the relationship when the child has grown into an adult.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
